---
title: "Data notes"
include-after-body: _search.html
---

```{r}
#| label: load
notes <- read.csv("../releases/data_notes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = "character")
notes <- notes[order(tolower(notes$table), notes$date, method = "radix"), ]
```

Some things a user of a table should know cannot be expressed by the table
itself: a covariate the source derived from the same detections and eco did not
ship, coordinates generalised for a threatened species, how a loss on capture is
encoded. eco reproduces its sources as released ([Corrections](corrections.qmd),
rule 6), so these are recorded as notes rather than fixed. Each note also appears
on the table's entry on [Browse the tables](data.qmd).

**What is listed here.** A note records something about a table that a careful
user would want before fitting a model to it and could not learn from the
columns. It is not a defect report: a table that does not match its source is
corrected in a new release, and released fixes are listed on
[Corrections](corrections.qmd). A table missing from this list has no note; that
does not mean its source is free of caveats, which the script that built it
states in its header.

The file is [`releases/data_notes.csv`](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/blob/main/releases/data_notes.csv),
appended by hand. `r nrow(notes)` notes cover `r length(unique(notes$table))`
tables. Start typing to search.

```{=html}
<input type="text" id="noteSearch" placeholder="Search notes..." oninput="filterRows('noteSearch', 'notes-table', 'note-count', 'note')" class="eco-search">
<p id="note-count" class="eco-search-count"></p>
```

::: {#notes-table .eco-searchable}

```{r}
#| label: notes
#| output: asis
cell <- function(x) gsub("|", "\\|", gsub("\n", " ", x), fixed = TRUE)
issue <- ifelse(grepl("^#[0-9]+$", notes$issue),
                sprintf("[%s](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/issues/%s)", notes$issue, sub("#", "", notes$issue)),
                notes$issue)
cat("| Table | Note | Issue | Added |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
cat(sprintf("| [`%s`](data.qmd#%s) | %s | %s | %s |", notes$table, notes$table, cell(notes$note), issue, notes$date), sep = "\n")
cat("\n")
```

:::
